content: 1. Secondary-level health facilities that provide otological and audiological services should be assessed every three years. This includes reviewing implementation reports, hospital reports, and relevant websites. The percentage of such facilities can be calculated by dividing the number of secondary-level facilities offering these services by the total number of secondary-level facilities in the country, multiplied by 100. 2. Primary-level health facilities providing ear and hearing care services should also be evaluated every three years. This involves analyzing implementation reports, hospital reports, and websites. The percentage is determined by dividing the number of primary-level facilities offering these services by the total number of primary-level facilities in the country, multiplied by 100. 3. The average age of intervention for children with hearing loss identified through hearing screening programs should be calculated every three years. This data is obtained from hospitals implementing infant hearing screening and early intervention programs. The national average is derived by averaging the data from all units (hospitals, states, or districts) implementing such programs. 4. The percentage of newborns screened through infant hearing screening programs can be estimated by dividing the number of infants screened by the total number of births in the country during the same time period, multiplied by 100. 5. The percentage of schools implementing hearing screening programs as part of school health services can be calculated by dividing the number of schools conducting hearing screenings by the total number of schools in the country (public, private, or both), multiplied by 100. 6. Tertiary-level health facilities providing otological and audiological services should be assessed. This includes facilities like medical colleges and referral hospitals offering routine ENT surgical services (e.g., myringotomy, ventilation tube insertion, tympanoplasty, mastoidectomy) and audiological services (e.g., pure tone audiometry, otoacoustic emission testing, auditory brainstem response testing, hearing aid fitting). The percentage is calculated by dividing the number of such facilities by the total number of tertiary-level facilities in the country, multiplied by 100. 7. The ratio of ENT specialists available per 100,000 population in urban and rural areas should be assessed every three years. This data can be obtained from certifying agencies, medical councils, or national ENT associations. The ratio is calculated by dividing the total number of ENT specialists by the total population, multiplied by 100,000. 8. The ratio of audiological professionals available per 100,000 population in urban and rural areas should also be assessed every three years. This data can be sourced from certifying agencies, audiological councils, or national associations of audiologists. The ratio is calculated by dividing the total number of audiological professionals by the total population, multiplied by 100,000. 9. The ratio of other trained personnel involved in ear and hearing care (e.g., ENT nurses, clinical officers) per 100,000 population in urban and rural areas should be assessed. This data can be obtained from certifying and registering agencies or Ministry of Health reports. The ratio is calculated by dividing the total number of trained personnel by the total population, multiplied by 100,000. 10. The percentage of primary-level doctors trained in ear and hearing care services should be calculated annually. This data is obtained from Ministry of Health training and implementation reports. The percentage is determined by dividing the number of trained doctors by the total number of primary-level doctors in the country, multiplied by 100. 11. The percentage of community-level health workers trained in ear and hearing care services should also be calculated annually. This data is sourced from Ministry of Health training and implementation reports. The percentage is determined by dividing the number of trained health workers by the total number of community-level health workers in the country, multiplied by 100. 12. The number of ENT specialists graduating annually per 100,000 population should be assessed every ten years. This data can be obtained from medical council registers or relevant certifying bodies. The ratio is calculated by dividing the total number of ENT specialists graduating annually by the total population, multiplied by 100,000. 13. The number of audiology professionals graduating annually per 100,000 population should also be assessed every ten years. This data can be sourced from certifying and registering agencies. The ratio is calculated by dividing the total number of audiology professionals graduating annually by the total population, multiplied by 100,000. 14. The percentage of the target population receiving immunization for rubella, meningitis, mumps, and measles should be calculated annually. This data is often available in Ministry of Health reports, child health department reports, or WHO country data. The percentage is determined by dividing the number of individuals immunized by the total target population, multiplied by 100. 15. The number of people fitted with hearing aids and/or cochlear implants as a percentage of persons with hearing loss, or as a ratio per 100,000 population, should be calculated annually. This data can be obtained from government or NGO reports. The percentage is determined by dividing the number of people fitted with devices by the total number of persons with hearing loss, multiplied by 100. 16. The number of children (aged 0–15) fitted with hearing aids and/or cochlear implants as a percentage of children with hearing loss, or as a ratio per 100,000 population aged 0–15 years, should be calculated annually. This data can be sourced from government or NGO reports. 17. The number of persons aged 15–60 fitted with hearing aids and/or cochlear implants as a percentage of persons with hearing loss in this age group, or as a ratio per 100,000 population aged 15–60 years, should be calculated annually. This data can be obtained from government or NGO reports. 18. The number of persons aged 60 or above fitted with hearing aids and/or cochlear implants as a percentage of persons with hearing loss in this age group, or as a ratio per 100,000 population aged above 60 years, should be calculated annually. This data can be sourced from government or NGO reports. 19. The number of persons receiving cochlear implants as a percentage of persons with hearing loss, or as a ratio per 100,000 population, should be calculated annually. This data can be obtained from government reports or cochlear implant companies.
